question: What Does It Mean To Be Serbian?

answers.text: Serbian yes
To love music and the food of course
World, world, help[she asked to be recorded]
Mother and son Sanja Jovanovic-Tanaskovic and Relja Tanaskovic please help
I am very, very proud because I am Serbian I am not... I am not racist Is it correct?
Unfortunately, at the moment there is no... gypsies, I respect, all all, all people
Proud Honest
Someone like Nikola Tesla
Someone like Novak Djokovic
Be smart
Be ready for everything
Hard worker
People here are very chill[She is from Russia]
Living a pretty relaxed life Especially compared to my country I like them and I really like Serbia in general
Have a certain level of hospitality that a lot of people that a lot of people don’t have
and also, I feel like we are really fun
And, I mean, there's a lot about things, but, yeah
To be proud to be Serbian
That is privileged to be Serbian
-what does it mean to be Montenegrin
to have your character, mentality and to be strong
To be honest to be proud and to have this inate do you know what this means? do you know what this means? when you are doing everything against, what they are expecting from you?
I was born in, Yugoslavia. So to me it was very hard. When Yugoslavia fell apart
I had to build my own Serbian identity basically after that
It is my home. But I respect all of the cultures here
It means to respect your past, your history, your culture your nature and everything else
well, maybe accepting it and, not trying to change the good things maybe only the bad
It's difficult to be Serbian in this times
There are pressures, everywhere for Serbians
we like Russia, we like America Yeah, I don’t know
Temperment,culture
but that goes for everyone
That you love Serbia Love Serbian... all the people who lives in Serbia not only Serbian people
to develop Serbia in a better way to be better
And I'm so sorry that my generation leaves to your generation and younger people, the situation in this country I would like if it could be fixed in some way
Being between... different cultures and trying to find your own identity in that space.
